# package gsdml

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-profinet/gsdml"
```

Package gsdml reads, validates and writes GSDML (General Station Description Markup Language) files, the XML device descriptions of PROFINET IO devices, and converts between them and the device models of package model.

The document types (zz\_generated.go) are generated from the catalog schema/catalog.json by internal/cmd/gengsdml; SCHEMA.md lists what they model. Elements and attributes the catalog does not define are kept in the Unknown and Attrs fields and written back, so reading and writing a file does not lose information. Comments and the order of unknown elements among known ones are not preserved.

The official GSDML schemas are licensed by PROFIBUS & PROFINET International to its members and are not part of this package; Validate checks the structural and lexical rules of the catalog and the references between elements, which covers what the device model relies on. It is not a substitute for PI's GSDML checker.

```go
const MaxDocumentSize = 64 << 20
```

MaxDocumentSize bounds the size of a document Parse reads. Vendor files reach 15 MB; the bound leaves room.

```go
const MaxModelRecordOctets = 16 << 20
```

MaxModelRecordOctets bounds the octets of all parameter records of the model ToModel builds, counted two ways: the records of the module types it converts, and the records of the device access point and of the modules as they are plugged, where a module in several slots counts once per slot. Beyond either, ToModel returns an error matching profinet.ErrResourceExhausted.

```go
const MaxRecordLength = 65535
```

MaxRecordLength bounds the length of a parameter record ToModel builds.

```go
const RuleSchema = "schema"
```

RuleSchema: the document is not valid against the GSDML schema of the version it names (gsdml/typed, generated from PI's reference schemas and checked against xmllint), or CheckBytes could not apply one (an unvalidated issue then says why).

### func ToModel

```go
func ToModel(doc *Document, dapID string) (*model.Device, error)
```

ToModel converts the device access point dapID (the first one when empty) of a document into a device model: the DAP, the modules that are fixed or used in slots, and the other usable modules as the catalog.

It returns an error matching profinet.ErrMalformed for a module or a device access point with more than 1440 submodules, which is more than a C\_SDU carries, and one matching profinet.ErrResourceExhausted for parameter records beyond MaxModelRecordOctets.

Submodules come from the VirtualSubmoduleList of the DAP and of each module. Configurable submodules (UseableSubmodules, SubmoduleItemRef) are not converted. One a configuration needs (FixedInSubslots or UsedInSubslots) fails ToModel with profinet.ErrUnsupported when it is the DAP's or a plugged module's; a module only in the catalog that needs one is left out of Catalog. Optional ones (only AllowedInSubslots) are left out of the model. A SubmoduleList no reference names does not matter. AnalyzeModels reports each with why (ModelReport.OmitsSubmodules, OmitsModules, ModuleReport.Omitted). NewConfiguration and Configuration.Resolve convert them.

### func Validate

```go
func Validate(doc *Document) error
```

Validate checks the document against the catalog's structural and lexical rules, checks that every ID is unique and every reference (module, submodule, value item, graphic, category and text references) resolves, and that no submodule's IO data exceed an RT frame. It returns nil or a \*ValidationError with the errors; Check reports the warnings and the unvalidated content as well.

## Types

### type Configuration

```go
type Configuration struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Configuration is a configuration of one device access point of a document: what NewConfiguration makes by default, changed by Plug, Unplug, Select and ClearSubslot, and turned into a model by Resolve. The default configuration plugs the modules ToModel plugs, in the slots it plugs them in, and places each configurable submodule in the subslots it is fixed or used in. Each plugged module has its own choices: two slots with the same module may hold different submodules.

A Configuration reads the document it was made from at every call; the document must not change while the Configuration is used. It is not safe for concurrent use.

#### func NewConfiguration

```go
func NewConfiguration(doc *Document, dapID string) (*Configuration, error)
```

NewConfiguration makes the default configuration of the device access point dapID (the first one when empty) of a document.

It returns the errors ToModel returns for the DAP and the modules it can use, except that configurable submodules are not refused: profinet.ErrNotFound for a DAP the document does not have, profinet.ErrMalformed for content that does not convert, for a reference whose subslot attributes are not ValueLists of subslot numbers (1 to 65535), and for configurable submodules of the DAP whose default subslots collide or lie outside its PhysicalSubslots, and profinet.ErrResourceExhausted beyond MaxModelRecordOctets. A configurable submodule or a module that cannot be placed is not an error here: its option carries why, and choosing it, or a default configuration that needs it, fails.

#### func (Configuration) ClearSubslot

```go
func (c *Configuration) ClearSubslot(slot, subslot uint16) error
```

ClearSubslot leaves a subslot of the module in a slot (of the DAP for slot 0) empty, removing the submodule it holds by default (UsedInSubslots) or by a Select. A slot without a module, subslot 0, the subslot of a virtual or system-defined submodule and a subslot a submodule is fixed in are errors matching profinet.ErrInvalidConfig.


DAP returns the configurable submodules of the device access point, in file order.

#### func (Configuration) Module

```go
func (c *Configuration) Module(slot uint16) (string, bool)
```

Module returns the ID of the module plugged in a slot.

#### func (Configuration) Modules

```go
func (c *Configuration) Modules() []ModuleOption
```

Modules returns the modules the device access point can use, one per ModuleItemRef, in file order.

#### func (Configuration) Plug

```go
func (c *Configuration) Plug(slot uint16, moduleID string) error
```

Plug plugs the module the DAP can use with ID moduleID into a slot, with its default submodules; a module the slot held is replaced, with the choices made for it. The slot must be 1 to 0x7FFF, in the DAP's PhysicalSlots and in the reference's AllowedInSlots (when it gives them), and must not hold a module fixed there (FixedInSlots) unless it is the same module. A module the DAP cannot use, a slot outside those, and a module that cannot be plugged (ModuleOption.Err) are errors matching profinet.ErrInvalidConfig; the configuration is then unchanged.

A module the DAP references more than once is plugged by the reference that applies to the slot: one that fixes or uses it there, else the first that allows it.

#### func (Configuration) PlugIdent

```go
func (c *Configuration) PlugIdent(slot uint16, ident uint32) error
```

PlugIdent is Plug for the module with ModuleIdentNumber ident. Two modules of the ident are an error matching profinet.ErrInvalidConfig that names them: plug one by ID.

#### func (Configuration) Resolve

```go
func (c *Configuration) Resolve() (*model.Device, error)
```

Resolve returns the model of the configuration: the DAP's identity, capabilities and submodules as ToModel builds them, with the chosen configurable submodules after the DAP's (a configurable port counts in Capabilities.Ports); the plugged modules with their virtual submodules and then their configurable ones in subslot order; and as the Catalog, per module reference in file order, the module with its default submodules, less those whose default does not resolve. Without configurable submodules it is ToModel's model.

It returns an error matching profinet.ErrInvalidConfig for a subslot that several submodules are used in by default and that no Select or ClearSubslot decided (the error names them), and for a model that model.Device.Validate refuses; a placed submodule's SubmoduleOption.Err; a module's ModuleOption.Err; and profinet.ErrResourceExhausted for parameter records of more than MaxModelRecordOctets in the plugged submodules.

#### func (Configuration) Select

```go
func (c *Configuration) Select(slot, subslot uint16, submoduleID string) error
```

Select puts the configurable submodule submoduleID of the module in a slot (of the DAP for slot 0) in a subslot, in place of the submodule the subslot holds by default (UsedInSubslots). It returns an error matching profinet.ErrInvalidConfig, and leaves the configuration unchanged, for a slot without a module, a submodule the module's UseableSubmodules do not name, subslot 0, the subslot of a virtual or system-defined submodule, a subslot another submodule is fixed in, a subslot the submodule is not allowed in (SubmoduleOption.Allows) or outside the PhysicalSubslots; and the option's Err for a submodule that cannot be placed.

The choices belong to the module plugged in the slot: plugging another module, or the same one again, starts from its defaults.

A submodule the UseableSubmodules reference more than once is chosen by the reference that applies to the subslot: one that fixes it there, else one that uses it there, else the first that allows it (those without an Err first). The references' attributes are not combined.

#### func (Configuration) Slots

```go
func (c *Configuration) Slots() []uint16
```

Slots returns the slots that hold a module, in ascending order.

#### func (Configuration) Unplug

```go
func (c *Configuration) Unplug(slot uint16) error
```

Unplug empties a slot. A slot without a module, and one whose module is fixed there, are errors matching profinet.ErrInvalidConfig.

Document is a parsed GSDML file.

#### func FromModel

```go
func FromModel(m *model.Device, opts GenerateOptions) (*Document, error)
```

FromModel generates a GSDML document that describes a device model: the identity, the DAP with its interface and ports, every module type with its submodules' IO data and parameter records, and the plugged modules as fixed in their slots. The document declares conformance class A and RT\_CLASS\_1, the scope this module implements. The result passes Validate.

#### func Parse

```go
func Parse(r io.Reader) (*Document, error)
```

Parse reads a GSDML document. UTF-8 (with or without a byte order mark) and ISO-8859-1 encodings are accepted. A document larger than MaxDocumentSize, or with more elements than ParseBytes reads, is refused with an error matching profinet.ErrResourceExhausted.

#### func ParseBytes

```go
func ParseBytes(data []byte) (*Document, error)
```

ParseBytes reads a GSDML document from data. A document with more than 1 048 576 elements is refused with an error matching profinet.ErrResourceExhausted before it is decoded.

### type Legality

```go
type Legality int
```

Legality says whether a schema version allows a DataType in a context.

```go
const (
	// LegalityUnverified: no audited schema decides it, because the
	// version was not audited (any version but the 18 from V1.0 to V2.46,
	// newer ones included) or its schema cannot decide the value.
	// It says nothing about whether the value is legal.
	LegalityUnverified Legality = iota
	// LegalityAllowed: the audited schema of the version allows it.
	LegalityAllowed
	// LegalityForbidden: the audited schema of the version does not allow
	// it, or does not have the context.
	LegalityForbidden
)
```

#### func DataTypeLegality

```go
func DataTypeLegality(version string, ctx DataTypeContext, dt DataType) Legality
```

DataTypeLegality says whether GSDML schema version version ("2.35", as Report.SchemaVersion gives it) allows dt in ctx. Only exact audited versions decide: nothing is inferred for a version between or after them, because a value can be removed and added again between versions.

The sets come from the schemas V1.0 to V2.46 as TIA Portal V21 installs them, a reserialised copy rather than PI's specification package (docs/research/GSDML-XSD-AUDIT.md), so Check reports a forbidden value as a warning, not an error. Legality is independent of a DataType's size (DataItemSize) and of whether ToModel can write its DefaultValue.

### type ModelReport

```go
type ModelReport struct {
	// DAP is the device access point's ID, and Path its element path.
	DAP  string `json:"dap"`
	Path string `json:"path"`
	// Outcome is always the classification of ToModel's error for the
	// DAP; Err is that error and Error its text, empty when it converted.
	// What else AnalyzeModels finds never changes them.
	Outcome Outcome `json:"outcome"`
	Error   string  `json:"error,omitempty"`
	Err     error   `json:"-"`
	// DAPErr is the error of the DAP's own content (identity,
	// capabilities, submodules), without its modules, and DAPError its
	// text; nil when that converts.
	DAPError string `json:"dap_error,omitempty"`
	DAPErr   error  `json:"-"`
	// Blocked reports that at least one of Modules has a reference or
	// module error: each one ToModel would refuse the DAP for, whichever
	// it reaches first. A DAP can be blocked and have another Outcome,
	// for example resource_exhausted when the plugged records exceed
	// MaxModelRecordOctets before ToModel reaches the reference.
	Blocked bool `json:"blocked"`
	// Modules are the DAP's UseableModules references, in file order.
	Modules []ModuleReport `json:"modules"`
	// ConfigurableSubmodules are the DAP's own UseableSubmodules
	// references, in file order. ToModel does not convert configurable
	// submodules: a required one is the DAP's DAPErr and fails it, an
	// optional one is left out of its model. Those of the modules are in
	// each ModuleReport; OmitsSubmodules reports both.
	ConfigurableSubmodules []SubmoduleRef `json:"configurable_submodules,omitempty"`
	// Model is ToModel's model when Outcome is OutcomeConverted, nil
	// otherwise: AnalyzeModels never returns a partial model.
	Model *model.Device `json:"-"`
}
```

ModelReport is what AnalyzeModels found for one device access point.

#### func AnalyzeModels

```go
func AnalyzeModels(doc *Document) ([]ModelReport, error)
```

AnalyzeModels converts every device access point of a document with ToModel and reports, for each, the outcome and why: every module reference gets its own status and that of the module it names, converted on its own, so that one that does not convert does not hide the others.

Configurable submodules (UseableSubmodules) are not converted by ToModel, which refuses a required one of the DAP or of a plugged module and leaves a module only in the catalog that needs one out of the catalog. The report lists every one with why (ConfigurableSubmodules, OmitsSubmodules, ModuleReport.Omitted, OmitsModules), so that a converted DAP that leaves something out is told from one that describes all of it.

It is a diagnostic: ToModel stays the conversion to use. A report's Outcome and Err are always ToModel's, and its Model is ToModel's, only for a DAP that converts.

A module several references name is converted once. It returns an error matching profinet.ErrMalformed for a nil document and for one without device access points.

#### func (ModelReport) OmitsModules

```go
func (r ModelReport) OmitsModules() bool
```

OmitsModules reports whether ToModel leaves a module the DAP references out of the model's Catalog (ModuleReport.Omitted): a converted DAP's catalog is then not every module the file lets it use.

#### func (ModelReport) OmitsSubmodules

```go
func (r ModelReport) OmitsSubmodules() bool
```

OmitsSubmodules reports whether the DAP or a module it references has configurable submodules (UseableSubmodules). ToModel converts none of them: it refuses a required one and leaves an optional one out of the model.

```go
	// one slot, when it converts.
	RecordOctets int `json:"record_octets"`
	// ConfigurableSubmodules are the UseableSubmodules references of the
	// module it names, in file order: submodules ToModel does not convert,
	// so the model's module has none of them.
	ConfigurableSubmodules []SubmoduleRef `json:"configurable_submodules,omitempty"`
	// Omitted reports that ToModel leaves the module out of the model's
	// Catalog: it needs a configurable submodule (ModuleOutcome
	// unsupported, ModuleErr why) and this reference plugs it in no slot.
	// An omitted module does not block the DAP; plugged, it would.
	Omitted bool `json:"omitted"`
}
```

ModuleReport is what AnalyzeModels found for one module reference of a device access point: the reference itself, and the module it names.

### type Outcome

```go
type Outcome string
```

Outcome is the result of converting a device access point or a module of a GSDML document to a model.

```go
const (
	// OutcomeConverted: converted as ToModel converts it.
	OutcomeConverted Outcome = "converted"
	// OutcomeMalformed: the description is not valid (an error matching
	// profinet.ErrMalformed, or any error not one of the others).
	OutcomeMalformed Outcome = "malformed"
	// OutcomeUnsupported: the content may be valid, but go-profinet does
	// not implement it (profinet.ErrUnsupported), for example a field
	// without a verified encoding.
	OutcomeUnsupported Outcome = "unsupported"
	// OutcomeResourceExhausted: the conversion went beyond a limit of
	// go-profinet (profinet.ErrResourceExhausted), for example
	// MaxModelRecordOctets.
	OutcomeResourceExhausted Outcome = "resource_exhausted"
	// OutcomeOmitted: valid, and left out of the model. Only a
	// SubmoduleRef has it: an optional configurable submodule, which
	// model.Device does not contain.
	OutcomeOmitted Outcome = "omitted"
)
```

The outcomes of AnalyzeModels.

### type ParameterConst

```go
type ParameterConst struct {
	ByteOffset uint32 `json:"byte_offset"`

}
```

ParameterConst is a Const of a parameter record: octets at an offset.

### type ParameterField

```go
type ParameterField struct {
	// ID is the Ref's ID, when it has one (from V2.3).
	ID string `json:"id,omitempty"`
	// Name is the text of TextId in the primary language, or TextId when
	// the file has no such text.
	Name     string   `json:"name"`
	DataType DataType `json:"data_type"`
	// ByteOffset is the offset of the field in the record. For Bit and
	// BitArea, BitOffset is the first bit in that octet (0 the least
	// significant) and BitLength the number of bits; they are 0 for the
	// other types.
	ByteOffset uint32 `json:"byte_offset"`
	BitOffset  uint8  `json:"bit_offset,omitempty"`
	BitLength  uint8  `json:"bit_length,omitempty"`
	// Length is the size of the field in octets: 0 for Bit and BitArea,
	// and for a DataType without a known size.
	Length int `json:"length,omitempty"`
	// Default and AllowedValues are as the file writes them; AllowedValues
	// is empty when the file does not restrict the value.
	Default       string `json:"default"`
	AllowedValues string `json:"allowed_values,omitempty"`
	// Changeable and Visible are reported. Set, a low-level encoder,
	// writes a field that is not Changeable; PlanParameters refuses a
	// value for it (Table D.31). Visible is not used.
	Changeable bool `json:"changeable"`
	Visible    bool `json:"visible"`
	// ValueItem is the Ref's ValueItemTarget, the ID of a ValueItem of
	// the file; empty when the Ref has none.
	ValueItem string `json:"value_item,omitempty"`
	// ValueItemMissing reports a ValueItemTarget that names no ValueItem
	// of the file. The field's permitted values are then not known: Set
	// refuses a value for it and Check reports it, rather than taking the
	// field as unrestricted.
	ValueItemMissing bool `json:"value_item_missing,omitempty"`
	// Values are the texts the file's ValueItem (ValueItemTarget) assigns
	// to values, in its order. Without AllowedValues they are the
	// permitted values; with neither, the DataType alone limits the value
	// (Siemens, GSDML Getting Started V1.10, 02/2024, section 15.2;
	// Table D.31 of ISO 15745-4:2003/Amd 1:2006, Annex D).
	Values []ParameterValue `json:"values,omitempty"`
	// Encodable reports whether Set can write the field: false for a
	// DataType without a verified encoding (the _S, composite, time and
	// PROFIdrive types), as for a DefaultValue in ToModel. It is reported
	// only: Set decides from DataType.
	Encodable bool `json:"encodable"`
}
```

ParameterField is a field of a parameter record (a Ref).

A field is plain data: Set writes it where its exported fields say, so a ParameterRecord read back from its JSON, or changed by its caller, encodes as it reads. Check reports a field whose Length or bits do not agree with its DataType, and Set refuses it.

BitOffset, BitLength, Changeable and Visible take the defaults of PI's GSDML schemas when the file does not give them: BitOffset 0, BitLength 1, Changeable and Visible true. These are the defaults of the Ref of a ParameterRecordDataItem in every schema V1.0 to V2.46 (ValueItemReferenceT in V1.0 to V2.1, ParameterRecordDataT/Ref in V2.2 and V2.25, RecordDataRefT from V2.3).

### type ParameterPlan

```go
type ParameterPlan struct {
	Writes []PlannedWrite `json:"writes"`
	// Issues are the records' Check issues and the plan's own, with
	// paths "Slot[s]/Subslot[0xSSSS]/ParameterRecordDataItem[i]/...".
	// Warnings and unvalidated issues do not stop a plan; the caller
	// decides whether the plan may be written. An unvalidated issue is
	// not evidence that a record is right.
	Issues []Issue `json:"issues"`
}
```

ParameterPlan is the parameter records to write to a device, in the order to write them, and what PlanParameters found on the way.

#### func PlanParameters

```go
func PlanParameters(doc *Document, m *model.Device, opts PlanOptions) (*ParameterPlan, error)
```

PlanParameters builds the parameter records to write to a device whose plugged modules m describes, from the file doc m was built from. It writes nothing: the plan is for controller.DeviceConfig.Parameters (converted with controller.Parameter(w.Write)) or for review.

  - The model must be of the file's device (VendorID and DeviceID) and DAP (ModuleIdentNumber).
  - Every plugged module must be one the DAP can use, in a slot of the DAP's PhysicalSlots and of the module's AllowedInSlots, and every plugged submodule must be in the file: a virtual submodule, or a configurable one (Configuration.Resolve) in a subslot its reference allows and within the PhysicalSubslots of its DAP or module. The DAP's interface and port submodules, built in or configurable, have no parameter records here: their PDev records are the controller's (PeerChecks, MRP).
  - Values may set only fields that are Changeable (Table D.31), each once: an ID and a name of one field are refused, rather than one of them winning by map order.
  - A record is written when PlanOptions.Values sets a field of it, or, with PlanOptions.Defaults, always. A record with values must build (ParameterRecord.Encode); a record written with its defaults only that cannot be built for a field without a verified encoding is left out and reported.
  - A written record with an error of ParameterRecord.Check refuses the plan; its warnings and unvalidated issues are reported.
  - The records of a submodule are written in ascending TransferSequence (1, 2, …, scoped to the submodule: Table D.28), then those of 0, an undefined order, in file order. Submodules are written in slot and subslot order, the DAP first: a policy of this package, not of Table D.28.

It returns an error matching profinet.ErrInvalidConfig for a model or values that do not match the file, a record that does not build or has a Check error, or TransferSequence values that are not 1 to N (unless AllowSequenceErrors); profinet.ErrNotFound for a DAP the file does not have; and profinet.ErrUnsupported for values in a record with a field without a verified encoding. With an error, the plan holds the issues found and no writes.

### type ParameterRecord

```go
type ParameterRecord struct {
	Index pnio.Index `json:"index"`
	// Name is the text of the record's Name in the primary language.
	Name   string `json:"name,omitempty"`
	Length uint16 `json:"length"`
	// TransferSequence is the order the record is written in; 0, the
	// schema default, when the file does not give one.
	TransferSequence uint16 `json:"transfer_sequence"`
	// Default is the record as ToModel built it (model.Record.Default)
	// when the record was described: zeros, the Const octets, then every
	// field's DefaultValue. It is nil when a field has no encoding this
	// package has verified. It is reported only: Encode builds the record
	// from Consts and Fields as they are, and Check reports a Default that
	// differs from that.
	Default []byte           `json:"default,omitempty"`
	Consts  []ParameterConst `json:"consts,omitempty"`
	Fields  []ParameterField `json:"fields"`
}
```

ParameterRecord describes a parameter record of a submodule as its GSDML file declares it (a ParameterRecordDataItem): its fields, its constant octets and its default value. Unlike model.Record it keeps what a value of a field must be, so that a record can be built from chosen values.

#### func SubmoduleParameters

```go
func SubmoduleParameters(doc *Document, dapID string, moduleIdent, submoduleIdent uint32) ([]ParameterRecord, error)
```

SubmoduleParameters describes the parameter records of a submodule: the submodule with ident number submoduleIdent of the device access point dapID (the first one when empty), when moduleIdent is the DAP's ModuleIdentNumber, or of the module with that ident number that the DAP can use. These are the submodules and records ToModel converts and, after them, the configurable submodules (a SubmoduleItem of the SubmoduleList the DAP's or module's UseableSubmodules name) that Configuration.Resolve converts.

It returns an error matching profinet.ErrNotFound when the DAP, the module or the submodule does not exist, and profinet.ErrMalformed for a record ToModel refuses as malformed. A field without a verified encoding is not an error: it is not Encodable, and its record has no Default.

#### func (ParameterRecord) Check

```go
func (r *ParameterRecord) Check() []Issue
```

Check reports what makes the record unfit to build records from, beyond the schema: see the RuleParameter rules. SubmoduleParameters already refuses a malformed layout or a DefaultValue that does not encode, so for its records Check reports overlaps, AllowedValues, and fields without a verified encoding; it checks a record from elsewhere (its JSON) in full. The issues' Path is "ParameterRecordDataItem\[index]/Ref\[i]" or ".../Const\[k]", with i and k counted from 0.

#### func (ParameterRecord) Encode

```go
func (r *ParameterRecord) Encode(values map[int]string) ([]byte, error)
```

Encode builds the record as ToModel does, from Consts and Fields as they are (zeros, the Const octets, every field's Default), and then sets the values of the fields given by their index, as Set does.

Encode encodes; it does not judge. A field's Default is written as the file gives it, also when Check warns that it is outside the field's AllowedValues, while a value given to Encode must be within them. What may be written to a device is the caller's decision, with Check.

It returns an error matching profinet.ErrUnsupported when a field has no verified encoding (the record cannot be built without it), and profinet.ErrInvalidConfig for a Const outside the record, a field or a Default that does not encode, or two given fields that share bits: which one would be written last is not a choice Encode makes.

#### func (ParameterRecord) Field

```go
func (r *ParameterRecord) Field(key string) (int, error)
```

Field returns the index of the field with ID key, or else of the only field with Name key. IDs exist from schema V2.3; a name is the text of the primary language, and two fields can share one. It returns an error matching profinet.ErrNotFound when no field has that ID or name, and profinet.ErrInvalidConfig when several fields have that ID, or that name and none that ID.

#### func (ParameterRecord) Set

```go
func (r *ParameterRecord) Set(rec []byte, i int, value string) error
```

Set writes value into the field i of rec, a record of r's Length: in the lexical form of a DefaultValue of the field's DataType ("12", "-3", "1.5", "true", "0x01,0x02" for an OctetString, a string as it is). The octets and bits outside the field are not changed. SetUint, SetInt, SetFloat, SetBool, SetString and SetBytes take Go values instead.

It returns an error matching profinet.ErrInvalidConfig for a value that does not fit the field, is outside its AllowedValues or, when it has none, is not a value its ValueItem assigns (Table D.31), and for a field whose Length or bits do not agree with its DataType; profinet.ErrUnsupported for a DataType without a verified encoding, an AllowedValues of a string or an OctetString (not compared) or beyond what is compared (see Check); and profinet.ErrMalformed for an AllowedValues that is not a SignedOrFloatValueListT, and for every value of a field whose ValueItemTarget names no ValueItem (ValueItemMissing).

#### func (ParameterRecord) SetBool

```go
func (r *ParameterRecord) SetBool(rec []byte, i int, v bool) error
```

SetBool writes v into the field i, a Boolean, as Set does.

#### func (ParameterRecord) SetBytes

```go
func (r *ParameterRecord) SetBytes(rec []byte, i int, v []byte) error
```

SetBytes writes v into the field i, an OctetString, as Set does: zero-padded to the field's Length, and refused when longer.

#### func (ParameterRecord) SetFloat

```go
func (r *ParameterRecord) SetFloat(rec []byte, i int, v float64) error
```

SetFloat writes v into the field i, a Float32 or a Float64, as Set does. For a Float32, v is rounded to the nearest Float32, and AllowedValues is compared with the rounded value, the one written.

#### func (ParameterRecord) SetInt

```go
func (r *ParameterRecord) SetInt(rec []byte, i int, v int64) error
```

SetInt writes v into the field i, an Integer8 to Integer64, as Set does.

#### func (ParameterRecord) SetString

```go
func (r *ParameterRecord) SetString(rec []byte, i int, v string) error
```

SetString writes v into the field i, a VisibleString or a UTF8String, as Set does: zero-padded to the field's Length, and refused when longer.

#### func (ParameterRecord) SetUint

```go
func (r *ParameterRecord) SetUint(rec []byte, i int, v uint64) error
```

SetUint writes v into the field i, an Unsigned8 to Unsigned64, a Bit or a BitArea, as Set does.

### type Report

```go
type Report struct {
	// SchemaVersion is the version the document declares (from
	// xsi:schemaLocation), empty when it declares none.
	SchemaVersion string  `json:"schemaVersion,omitempty"`
	Issues        []Issue `json:"issues"`
}
```

Report is the result of Check: every issue, with its severity.

#### func Check

```go
func Check(doc *Document) Report
```

Check validates a document against the catalog (as Validate does) and the semantic rules, and lists the content it did not validate. Nothing it reports makes it PI's GSDML checker.

The report is bounded: Check lists the first 16 384 issues of each severity, and one more issue of that severity with the rule "limit" then says how many it left out; a module reference gets at most eight warnings per slot list and rule and an interface at most eight per reduction ratio list, each followed by one that counts the rest; an ID in the path of an issue of the semantic rules is quoted up to 256 octets. The slot rules look at the slot numbers 0 to 65535: a list is warned about once for the values above them.

#### func CheckBytes

```go
func CheckBytes(data []byte) (Report, error)
```

CheckBytes reads a GSDML document and checks it as Check does, with one difference: the structure (required and allowed elements and attributes, their order and number, lexical forms and facets, and the identity constraints, key, keyref and unique, in their scopes) is validated against the schema of the version the document names, by gsdml/typed, instead of the catalog's version-independent rules, and so are the references (the schema's keyrefs, in their scopes, replace the catalog's global ID table, which misses IDs in elements the catalog does not model). Those issues have the rule RuleSchema and the line of the element. The physical-limit and semantic rules of Check apply as before.

A document that names no version typed has (none, or one newer than V2.46) is checked against the catalog, as Check does, and an unvalidated issue with the rule RuleSchema says so.

The error is that of ParseBytes: the document is not well-formed or exceeds a limit. The original octets are validated, not a re-encoding: Marshal writes the catalog's form (defaults, the newest element order), which is not valid against every older version.

#### func (Report) Count

```go
func (r *Report) Count(s Severity) int
```

Count returns the number of issues of a severity.

#### func (Report) Err

```go
func (r *Report) Err() error
```

Err returns the errors of the report as a \*ValidationError, or nil.

### type Severity

```go
type Severity int
```

Severity grades an issue of a GSDML document.

```go
const (
	// SeverityError: the document breaks a rule of the catalog (structure,
	// lexical form, references) or a physical limit; Validate fails.
	SeverityError Severity = iota
	// SeverityWarning: the document is valid for the catalog but probably
	// wrong; the rule says whether it is publicly substantiated or a local
	// heuristic of go-profinet.
	SeverityWarning
	// SeverityUnvalidated: content outside go-profinet's catalog (newer
	// schema versions, vendor extensions); kept as read, not checked.
	SeverityUnvalidated
)
```




### type SubmoduleOption

```go
type SubmoduleOption struct {
	// ID is the reference's SubmoduleItemTarget: the ID of the item.
	ID string `json:"id"`
	// Port reports a PortSubmoduleItem: a port of the DAP's interface.
	// It has no IO data and no records here; its PDev records are the
	// controller's, as for a built-in port.
	Port bool `json:"port,omitempty"`
	// Submodule is the submodule as the model holds it, converted as
	// ToModel converts a VirtualSubmoduleItem (name, ident number, API, IO
	// data lengths, parameter records with their defaults), with Subslot
	// 0: the configuration places it.
	Submodule model.Submodule `json:"submodule"`
	// AllowedInSubslots, UsedInSubslots and FixedInSubslots are the
	// reference's attributes as the file gives them.
	AllowedInSubslots string `json:"allowed_in_subslots,omitempty"`
	UsedInSubslots    string `json:"used_in_subslots,omitempty"`
	FixedInSubslots   string `json:"fixed_in_subslots,omitempty"`
	// Defaults are the subslots the default configuration puts the
	// submodule in (FixedInSubslots, else UsedInSubslots); Fixed reports
	// that they are fixed.
	Defaults []uint16 `json:"defaults,omitempty"`
	Fixed    bool     `json:"fixed,omitempty"`
	// Err is why the submodule cannot be placed, nil when it can, and
	// Error its text: a reference to no item of the SubmoduleList, an item
	// that does not convert (ErrMalformed, ErrUnsupported,
	// ErrResourceExhausted, as ToModel classifies them), a DAP submodule
	// of an API other than 0 or a port of a module (ErrUnsupported).
	Err   error  `json:"-"`
	Error string `json:"error,omitempty"`

}
```

SubmoduleOption is a configurable submodule a device access point or a module can use: a SubmoduleItemRef of its UseableSubmodules and the SubmoduleItem or PortSubmoduleItem of the SubmoduleList it names.

#### func (SubmoduleOption) Allows
